tone_statements.quote: Il se dégage de cette analyse que la langue äéàbóöt atteste trois tons ponctuels. Il s’agit du ton haut, moyen, et bas. D’après notre analyse, les tons haut et bas sont des tons sous-jacents c’est à dire des tons de la structure profonde de la langue. Par contre, le ton moyen provient de deux processus phonologiques. Le premier processus qui assigne le ton moyen est la règle de Meeussen adaptée à la langue äéàbóöt. Cette règle stipule que si deux tons haut sont adjacents sur une unité lexicale, le second ton haut devient moyen.
tone_statements.translation: It emerges from this analysis that the äéàbóöt [Bebot] language attests three level tones: high, mid and low. According to our analysis, the high and low tones are underlying tones, i.e. tones of the deep structure of the language. The mid tone, by contrast, comes from two phonological processes. The first process assigning mid tone is Meeussen's rule adapted to Bebot. This rule states that if two high tones are adjacent on a lexical unit, the second high tone becomes mid.
tone_statements.locator: p. 161, Chapitre VII: Conclusion générale; cf. ch. VI §6.0 p. 106 and ch. VI summary p. 157
tone_statements.n_tones: 3 surface level tones (H, M, L; H and L underlying) + contour combinations

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal, Pierre Nougayrol & Pierre Palayer. 2006. Lexique comparatif historique des langues sara-bongo-baguirmiennes (document électronique). Paris: CNRS-LLACAN (UMR 8135). Online database (c. 1,319 comparative series with reconstructions and consonant/vowel/tone correspondence formulas).
sources.note: Presentation page (read): tone-marked bdj forms in every series; tone schemes coded with two digits on a register scale (2-register H=3/B=1, 3-register H=3 M=2 B=1, 4-register incl. infra-low 0); each series carries tonal correspondence formulas at three successive proto-levels *SBB, *OCC, *SARA; the 'occidental' languages incl. all Sara languages share the *OCC innovation of a third tone register; nominal formulas *11/*12/*21a/*21b/*22 (original) vs *31/*32/*13/*23 (remade at *OCC); five original verbal tone-class formulas. Genealogy adopted from Boyeldieu 2000's tonal comparison.

tone.n_tones: 3 registers for the Sara languages incl. 'bedjond (coding H=3, M=2, B=1)
